statements.text: The two points A(3, 0), B(-1, 0) are both located on the x-axis, so AB = |-1 - 3| = |-4|, so AB = 4 unit length. Formula: $AB=|-1-3|=|-4|=4$
The two points C(0, -3), D(0, -1) are both located in the y-axis, so CD = |-3 - (-1)| = |-3 + 1| = |-2|, CD = 2 unit length. Formula: $CD=|-3-(-1)|=|-3+1|=|-2|=2$

The points M(3, 2), N(7, 5) are represented graphically in the figure. To find the length of MN: MK = |7 - 3| = 4 unit length, NK = |5 - 2| = 3 unit length. Triangle MKN is right angled at K, therefore (MN)^2 = (MK)^2 + (KN)^2 (Pythagoren theory), (MN)^2 = (3)^2 + (4)^2, (LM)^2 = 9 + 16, (MN)^2 = 25, therefore MN = 5 unit length. Formula: $(MN)^2=(MK)^2+(KN)^2=3^2+4^2=25, \ MN=5$
The distance between two points $(x_1, y_1)$, $(x_2, y_2)$ equals $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$.
The distance between two points = the square root of (square of the difference in the x-axis + square of the difference in the y-axis).
The distance of a point $M(x_1, y_1)$ from the origin point $O(0, 0)$ is $OM=\sqrt{x_1^2+y_1^2}$.
